nodes.summary: Setting every variable true with probability $1/2$, the closed-form satisfaction probability of a clause with $k$ literals is $1 - 2^{-k}$; for a clause whose literals use distinct variables this is the probability that it is satisfied. This is the analysis of Johnson's algorithm that Goemans and Williamson recall in §2: it is good for long clauses and poor for unit clauses.

nodes.summary: For every truth assignment $a$, the incidence vectors $y_i = [a_i]$ and $z_j = [a \text{ satisfies } C_j]$ are feasible for (LP), with objective $\sum_j w_j z_j$ equal to the weight satisfied by $a$. Hence the optimal value of (LP) is at least the MAX SAT optimum, $Z^*_{LP} \ge Z^*_{IP}$.
nodes.title: Truth assignments are feasible for the relaxation

nodes.summary: For clauses $C_1, \ldots, C_m$, a pair $(y, z)$ is feasible for (LP) when $0 \le y_i \le 1$ for every variable, $0 \le z_j \le 1$ and $z_j \le \sum_{i \in P_j} y_i + \sum_{i \in N_j}(1 - y_i)$ for every clause. The objective is $\sum_j w_j z_j$. The Lean definition imposes $0 \le y_i \le 1$ on all variable indices, which costs nothing since unused variables can be set to $0$.

Then the closed-form satisfaction probability of $C$ under $p_i = y_i$ is at least $\beta_k z$. can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
